> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4008e6290f4812b1c18a42ec2589b8a2733cf6c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa9f0d69a1d2fb69324e8122a04581bb9b8c31e8` — the merge of head `85261a810dff62b530193fbe92e7b607158a76d3` into base `4008e6290f4812b1c18a42ec2589b8a2733cf6c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa9f0d69a1d2fb69324e8122a04581bb9b8c31e8 && git checkout fa9f0d69a1d2fb69324e8122a04581bb9b8c31e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4008e6290f4812b1c18a42ec2589b8a2733cf6c3 85261a810dff62b530193fbe92e7b607158a76d3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4008e6290f4812b1c18a42ec2589b8a2733cf6c3 && git merge --no-ff 85261a810dff62b530193fbe92e7b607158a76d3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4008e6290f4812b1c18a42ec2589b8a2733cf6c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4008e6290f4812b1c18a42ec2589b8a2733cf6c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a15f252f6ae1bad0978ae63469a9b13f29caf712`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.named-base-overlay-write.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/package-commit-revert-path-package.dogfood.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-row-bindings.ts (resolveOverlayPackageBinding), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (restoreVersion, whereFor), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commit-record.ts (recordPackageCommit), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the commit revert, rollback and package revert doors), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (NOT_OVERRIDABLE), docs/adr/0146 D1 and D11, docs/adr/0067 D3, .changeset/28905-named-base-overlay-write-closed.md (the #28905 close, PR #29270 at 838a802b), protocol.ts rollbackMetaItemUnaudited and the publishPackageDrafts commit-plan read (lines 17501-17512 on the head)

### ① Derived judgments

Read on the head's tree, `git diff origin/main...pr29632` (fa07650b...a15f252f), 5 files, +246/-12.

- **Which items now refuse — right.** Only the restore limb of `revertCommit` (`it.existedBefore && it.prevVersion !== null`), and only when `namedBaseCloseSubject` answers a pair: the row's binding (`resolveOverlayPackageBinding`) is a READ-ONLY package among `overlayBaseShippers(type, name)` (so one of the five overlay types, else `[]`), the pair id forms, the ensure door would not refuse, the base records a version, and the override write gate admits the declared body. Every other restore stays as on main: the soft-remove limb (`!it.existedBefore`, never reaches the new lines), a row of the pair (the pair is not a shipper of the name), a writable package, a package-less row (binding `null` returns before any read), and every fix the pair cannot take. Matches the seat ruling (A, A1, per item) exactly.
- **Key checked = key written — right.** `resolveOverlayPackageBinding(it.type, it.name, member)` reads `sys_metadata` with `{type, name, state:'active', member-where}` and returns that row's `package_id`; `SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` reads its active row with `whereFor(ref, 'active', undefined, member)`, the same four predicates, and threads that row's `package_id` into `put`. Same table, same predicate shape, same member handling; the stored spelling (`it.type`) is used for both row reads and the singular (`PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[it.type] ?? it.type`) only for the registry-side subject, exactly as `rollbackMetaItemUnaudited` (binding read on `singularType`, subject on `singularType`). Where the two rows disagree at all is the any-package coin toss both share (card #29414), not a key mismatch introduced here.
- **One predicate, one sentence — right.** The door calls the class method `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal(subject, 'rollback')`, which is `namedBaseCloseSubject` + the module's `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal` emitter; the `'rollback'` arm's text ("a rollback of its row bound to the read-only base is closed (ADR-0146 D1, D11): save the version's body into PAIR, declaring overrides ...") is the one `rollbackMetaItem` already answers. No new string, no new code, no new status. `NamedBaseWriteSubject.member?: string` accepts `...memberOption(member)`; `item` absent means the subject is judged on `{name, member-discriminator}` + overrides, as the per-item rollback is judged.
- **A refused item writes nothing — right.** The throw sits after the binding read and before `repo.restoreVersion`, inside the existing per-item `try`: no `put`, no history event, no `applyRegistryWriteThrough`, no projector, no mutation emit. The catch maps it with `clientFacingFailureCode`: `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` is a member of `ErrorCode` (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, lines 690/1241/1295), so the code passes through untouched, and `clientFacingFailureText` keeps a 403 authored sentence whole. The item lands in `failed[]` with `{type, name, error, code:'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'}`; the loop continues to the next item; `success` is `failed.length === 0 && reverted.length > 0`. This is the channel `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `ITEM_LOCKED`, `STORED_TYPE_NOT_CANONICAL` (#9174) and the #25278 family already ride; the REST door (`packages.ts` 2421-2442) wraps the result in `deps.success(result)` whatever `success` says, so the wire shape is 200 with `success:false` as before for any per-item failure.
- **Revert commit still recorded — right, with one shape to know.** `recordPackageCommit` is called unconditionally with `items: reverted.map(...)`; the refused item is absent from it, so the revert commit never claims it. For a commit whose ONLY item is refused, a zero-item `revert` commit is recorded (the host function has no empty-items guard) and `rollbackToPackageCommit` still lists it in `revertedCommits` — the behaviour the rollback docblock already declares ("the step still ... records its revert commit, so that commit is also listed") and the behaviour `STORED_TYPE_NOT_CANONICAL` already produces on main. Not changed by this PR; named so the ledger shape is known.
- **rollbackToPackageCommit on a refused item — report and continue, right; no loop, no double revert, no worse partial state.** Its loop filters `apply` commits strictly newer than the target, skips `revert` commits, calls `revertCommit` once per commit and copies each `step.failed[]` entry as `Item 'TYPE/NAME' was not reverted: ...`; `success` is `failed.length === 0`. A refused item leaves the `apply` commit in place, so a second rollback re-refuses it (idempotent, finite). The per-commit mixed outcome (neighbours reverted, the base-bound row kept at its current version and still served) is the same partial shape every per-item refusal of this channel already leaves, and it replaces a write the published spec forbids; before the change every package rollback replayed the pre-close commits onto the base-bound row (measured by the dev, 7f277a86), which was the worse state.
- **protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts — JSDoc only.** The +8/-5 is inside the docblock of `NamedBaseWriteOperation` (the `'rollback'` operation is now described as every restore of a stored version, the per-item rollback and the commit revert's restore limb). The type alias, both emitters, `closedOverlayWriteClauses`, `namedBaseCloseSubject` and `packagelessCloseSubject` are byte-unchanged, so no caller's answer moves.
- **The dev's flagged consequence (a pair commit beside a pre-close base row) — a correct refusal of the write that would have happened, not a new false refusal of a correct one.** The plan read (`publishPackageDrafts`, head lines 17501-17512) and the restore both read ANY package's active row; when that read lands on the base-bound row, the write the restore would perform is the base-bound row rewritten with the base's own snapshot — exactly the write #28905 closes — so refusing it under the same key is right, and it replaces a `success:true` over nothing written (measured). When the read lands on the pair's row the restore proceeds as before. The addressing defect is the real bug and is filed as #29414 (open, ruled serial after this card). The sentence names the pair as the destination, which for an operator already in the pair reads oddly but is loud and actionable, and no previously correct outcome is lost.
- **Tests.** The five unit cases drive the real `saveMetaItem` + `publishPackageDrafts` + `revertCommit` + `rollbackToPackageCommit` over the file's existing stub engine, shadowing the instance's close only while producing the pre-close commits and asserting the close is live again before the revert; fake `Date` only, released in `afterEach`. The dogfood case does the same through REST on the booted showcase, runs last, and ends by reverting the creation commit so the shipped document is served again (the preceding pair case removes its own pair row, so no declared override masks the base-bound row). Controls cover the soft-remove limb, the writable package (#6215 shape) and the pair's own commit.

### ② Semver level

- Package moved: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` only (no `packages/spec` path in the file list). Changeset `.changeset/29390-named-base-commit-revert-closed.md` bumps that package `patch`.
- Declaration lines, both in the PR body and the changeset, line-initial and exactly once each (grep on the fetched body and on `git show pr29632:.changeset/...`): the ② key reads
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
and `Metadata-protocol: none`. One occurrence of the key in each document, so the level axis is MEASURED. The form is the one AGENTS.md admits (`no` plus the `(narrowing)` arm, which is BREAKING), so: `!` on the PR title and the changeset title (both present), a **BREAKING** banner (present, "write narrowing at the commit doors, shipped as patch"), FROM → TO migration (present: the revert now answers per-item refusal; TO is the declared write into the pair, or the delete naming the base), and one `adr-0087:` marker.
- Level: `none` on the metadata-protocol axis takes `patch` ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). `none` is right: what an author can write is unchanged against main; the five-type flag already stopped opening the write naming the base in #28905's changeset (which declared `narrowed` and `minor` for that reason). This diff closes a residual door on the same rows and introduces no key, value or requirement change. Consistent with the seat's claim.
- ADR-0087 marker: `not-required (already-registered packageless-overlay-write-closed)`. The id resolves at HEAD and at the merge base (`origin/main:packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts`, line 19), so the category is the honest one (the gate's rule: exists at base ⇒ `already-registered`, never `registered`). Fit: the entry's `replacement` is this change's TO (write the customization into the base's `.custom` pair with the `overrides` declaration; `os migrate packageless-overlays --apply` moves bound rows too since #29477), and no stored row is rewritten, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to do. **S1 (should-fix, text):** the marker's `why` repeats #29270's sentence "The entry's surface names the package-less write only; widening its text is a packages/spec edit this change does not make" — stale on main since 1bdf674e (#29535), which widened the entry to BOTH meta-door addresses (package-less and naming the read-only package, including "a rollback of a row bound to the package"). What the entry still does not name is the commit doors (`POST /api/v1/packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert`, `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/rollback`) as a third address of the same close. The disposition stands; the sentence should be corrected and the entry widening carded to the spec lane (text only). Not a FAIL: the category, id and TO are right and the gate (Check Changeset, dispatch-gates 65/65) reads the arm and the kind, not the prose.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: completed, success (both runs).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Lines kept in protocol.ts (dev freeze note) — right, and not a second spelling either way.** `revertCommit` is at protocol.ts line 19901 on the head; the #25467 E2 cuts (1a: 85f77e93, list/audit/UI-view reads; 1b: e9d95490, item and layered reads) moved no commit door. The predicate and the emitter live in `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`; the call site lives in the door, as `rollbackMetaItemUnaudited`'s does. Moving the call into the module would have required a second copy of the binding read or a second host, which is what the dev refused. One predicate (`namedBaseCloseSubject`), one sentence; the door-side nine code lines are a call and a throw.
- **Forced prose edit of the dogfood header — right and required.** Main's header (the #29090 file, closed card) says "one recorded before keeps its revert, as the commit doors still take no read-only guard"; after this change that is true of the soft-remove limb only. Leaving it would make the header a false statement about the file's own last case. No assertion changed; the PR body names the edit, as the ruling asked.
- **Body footer deviation** — the dev placed the harness attribution before the repo footer; the seat patched the body at 22:45Z to drop the duplicate, no other change (one footer remains, "Card thread session ... / Generated by Claude Code"). `PR-body guards` completed success on the head. Nothing further.
- **Dogfood readings — judged as reported, the only dogfood reading on this head** (the `Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix)` shards are skipped on pull_request; the aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate` reads success). Dev's local full battery on a15f252f: Test Files 398 passed / 3 skipped (401), Tests 3281 passed / 28 skipped, VERDICT command-exit 0; the earlier 4 reds on ecf913ed/d776e258 (flow-runas, declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest) were red on the control leg too and fixed on main by #29451, which a15f252f carries. Ablation on ecf913ed (close dropped from the restore limb): unit 2 failed / 20 passed, dogfood 1 failed / 7 passed, blob restored to HEAD. **Verified with git that the code under test is unchanged since ecf913ed:** the PR's own hunk lines for all five files are byte-identical between `f72bc9e5..ecf913ed` and `0ab4a09e..a15f252f`; and each merge commit is a clean merge (`git merge-tree --write-tree` of its two parents reproduces its tree: ecf913ed = 135fc5ef, d776e258 = 339e27cf, a15f252f = 1474a459), so no hand edit rode a merge. The ablation reading transfers.
- **open_questions:** the first report's three (the fork, the key, the channel) are each answered by ruling 6579511992 (A, A1, per item); the final report carries none. All answered.
- **Seat's out-of-scope rulings — confirmed, with one escalation:**
  - Any-package plan/restore lookup → #29414 (open, filed, serial after this card). Confirmed; see ① on why A1 is still the right interim.
  - `packages.ts` revert-door comment wording → confirmed out of this card's surface, and marginal: the literal "stays open" sentence the dev quotes is not in the file on main; the #22113 comment at `POST /packages/:id/revert` (line 2503) describes `revertStoredPackage`, which discards drafts and restores nothing, so it stays true; the commit doors' comment (2418-2420, "edited ones are restored to their pre-commit version") stays true in general with a per-item refusal beneath it. Word it when #29414 touches the file.
  - The restore limb's package-less close → confirmed out of this card's ruled scope (the card names the #28905 close), but **S2 (should-fix, escalate):** the dev's class-b finding understates the reach. A package-less row is reached not only through the any-package lookup: when the base-bound row an edit commit touched has since been removed (the open delete naming the base), the restore limb finds no active row, `resolveOverlayPackageBinding` answers `null`, neither close is asked, and `restoreVersion` INSERTS an unbound row with the pre-commit body ("a missing active row yields null — the unbound row"). That is the package-less write #28576 closes, and `rollbackMetaItemUnaudited` refuses it on the same `null` binding through `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal`. Pre-existing on main, not widened by this PR, no assertion today. It belongs on #29414 or its own card with this path named.
- **Check-runs on a15f252f at review time:** 29 completed success (among them Check Changeset x2, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, the four scoped lint gates, Type Check · source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger and workspace, Build Core, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core 2/8 and 6/8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards x2, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs); 15 completed skipped (path-filtered UI/docs/dogfood shards/opt-in harnesses); **still in progress: Test Core 1/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 7/8, 8/8.** The dev's local readings for those families (metadata-protocol 22251 passed, objectql 10488 passed, dispatch-gates 65/65) are the only measure of them on this head so far; the landing rule's "every check green" still has to be read off the runs when they finish.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Against the published spec on main.** ADR-0146 D1: on an item of a read-only package, "rollback, source save, reset and delete are offered only on the writable package"; D11 Close: "rollback onto a read-only package's item ... offered only on the writable package" after the migration. #28905 (PR #29270, 838a802b) implemented that at the save, publish and per-item rollback doors and declared it in its changeset and the `packageless-overlay-write-closed` entry (which, since #29535, names "a rollback of a row bound to the package" as closed). A commit revert's restore limb is a rollback onto that row by another door, reached through `repo.restoreVersion` with no close asked. This PR makes the spec's own refusal real at that door; it closes a bypass of an already-declared close, which is what the card asks under option (a).
- **Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. ADR-0067 D3 declares `revertCommit` / `rollbackToPackageCommit` restore each item to its pre-commit body through `restoreVersion`; the per-item `failed[]` channel is already how that door reports a restore it must not perform, and ADR-0146 (later, superseding in part) decides which writes onto a read-only package's items exist at all. The only statement that "a commit recorded before keeps its revert" was test header prose (#29090), not a spec. The capability ADR-0146 does keep for such a row — removing it — is kept here (soft-remove limb untouched, delete naming the base untouched), and every writable destination keeps its revert in place (the #6215 control). Nothing declared-and-undelivered is being hidden by a narrowing: the refusal is loud, coded and prescriptive, and the pre-close rows stay served. Not a consumer-side `??`; the close is asked at the write door on the row's own binding, the producer side of the row.
- **Attempts to break it, read in the live tree:**
  1. Mixed commit (object + base-bound view): the view is refused, the object restored, the revert commit lists the object only; a re-run restores the object again and re-refuses the view — the existing channel's idempotency, nothing new.
  2. Member-bearing type (`email_template` locale): `member` flows into the subject and into `whereFor`; `namedBaseCloseSubject` judges the declared body at that member, refusing the close (leaving the write open) where the base ships no such locale — the #28905 carve-out carries over unchanged.
  3. Legacy plural at rest: refused earlier by `isNonCanonicalStoredType` (#9174); `objects` folds but is not an overlay type, so `overlayBaseShippers` is `[]`.
  4. A refusal is logged with `console.warn` by the shared catch — the channel's existing shape for every authored 4xx it collects; no audit row, as the door writes none for any per-item failure (#9174 reasoning).
  5. `POST /packages/:id/revert` (`revertStoredPackage`) discards drafts and never calls `restoreVersion` — not a fourth restore door.
  6. Cluster write-through replay and `rollbackMetaItem` read `resolveOverlayPackageBinding` unchanged.
  7. Coexisting pair row + base-bound row and the vanished-binding insert: see ① and ③ — the former is a correct refusal of the write the lookup picked (#29414), the latter is the pre-existing package-less sibling (S2). Neither is introduced or widened here.
- **Findings:** no must-fix. Should-fix S1 (stale marker sentence; entry does not yet name the commit doors — spec-lane text) and S2 (the restore limb's package-less sibling reaches an unbound INSERT through the deleted-row path; escalate onto #29414 or a card of its own). Observation, no fix: the zero-item revert commit for a wholly refused apply commit is the channel's declared contract.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · PR #29632 · 2026-11-02T23:34Z

Head-sha: `85261a810dff62b530193fbe92e7b607158a76d3`

**维护者速读(席位终稿)**
- **改了什么**:按提交撤销(`POST /packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert`)和整包回滚(`POST /packages/:id/rollback`)时，如果要把旧版本恢复进绑定只读基础包本身的那一行，现在逐项拒绝。被拒的项进 `failed[]`,`code: NOT_OVERRIDABLE`,提示与逐项回滚是同一句：改写进 `.custom` 配对包，并声明 `overrides`。被拒的项什么都不写，同一提交的其它项照常撤销。判定复用 #28905 的同一谓词和同一句，没有第二种写法。
